summary: Redwood demo of Console per-route telemetry and cost breakdown for LatticeAI. Focus on usage analytics, route tagging, and cost attribution options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer concerned about latency/cost tradeoffs, data residency and SSO/KMS integration. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, pilot kick-off.

Audit logs, SAML and KMS integration
transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we know you booked 50 minutes so we'll try to keep it tight. I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Evelyn, our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Maya Singh: hi jamie, thanks. i have tom and priya here, we'll hop in as needed.
[00:12] Tom Reeves: morning, yeah, excited to see the console level stuff. we mostly care about per-route cost and detecting anomalies.
[00:18] Evelyn Chen: great, quick agenda — show per-route dashboards, dig into cost decomposition (tokens, model, infra), and then a short dive into routing policies and a private deployment checklist. we'll leave 10 minutes for q&a. sound good?
[00:28] Priya Nair: sounds good.
[00:31] Jamie Park: alright jumping in — i'm sharing screen, you should see the Redwood Console home, quick note: this is the sandbox org so numbers are scrubbed.
[00:40] [00:40] Evelyn Chen: so first thing you'll notice is the Usage Overview, top row shows total tokens by week, average latency, and cost per 1k tokens. below that we have the Routes table — each route is a logical endpoint you define in your app. in your pilot we'd recommend mapping the 3 highest-traffic API routes to separate Redwood routes so you get clean attribution.
[00:58] Maya Singh: quick q — can we tag routes automatically from our gateway? we use envoy + custom headers.
[01:04] Evelyn Chen: yes, you can pass a route tag header or use our SDK to set route on the request. we also support auto-parse from path patterns if you prefer.
[01:11] Tom Reeves: and that'll show up in the dashboard historically? like retro attribution?
[01:15] Evelyn Chen: for new data yes; for retro you'd need to re-ingest logs or run an export-ingest job, we can help with that in the pilot.
[01:21] Jamie Park: moving to the Route Detail — i'm opening the route for your chat completion path. top chart is tokens/sec and cost over time, you can debounce to hourly/daily.
[01:31] [01:31] Evelyn Chen: notice the cost breakdown on the right — model compute, GPU infra, and token billing. model compute is a function of sequence length distribution and chosen variant; infra is impacted by concurrency and batching.
[01:41] Priya Nair: we've been seeing token spikes because users paste long docs, any immediate levers?
[01:45] Evelyn Chen: short term: truncate with a system prompt, set max tokens per call, or enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. longer term: model selection and quantization — smaller model variant for high-volume, non-critical routes.
[01:55] Maya Singh: you mentioned prefix cache — is that the KV cache? we've seen mention of KV cache in your docs but unclear how it affects cost.
[02:02] Evelyn Chen: yep KV cache — it stores previously computed key/value attention state for repeated prefixes. In practice it reduces tokens sent and compute for subsequent calls, lowering effective per-call cost. The dashboard simulates the cost delta if cache hit rates increase.
[02:15] Tom Reeves: does KV cache require sticky sessions or can it be shared across pods?
[02:20] Evelyn Chen: it's part of the runtime; cache can be local or distributed depending on deployment. with Redwood Dedicated, cache is co-located and highly efficient; with hosted we do cross-instance cache and it's transparent.
[02:30] Jamie Park: jumping to the Cost Explorer — you can filter by model, route, team, or tag. here's a quick compare: same route served by gpt-3.2-ish model vs a 7B quantized variant — you can see the cost-per-1k tokens drop 3x and the latency increases ~40 ms.
[02:47] [02:47] Priya Nair: that's helpful. what about quality monitoring? we can't just drop to a smaller model without checks.
[02:53] Evelyn Chen: agreed — Redwood Optimize includes evals and regression alerts. you can upload a prompt set and have automated quality comparisons between model versions. we'll surface drift and a pass/fail threshold.
[03:05] Maya Singh: security — we have to stay in-region for data residency and use our KMS. how does Redwood handle encryption and key management for Private?
[03:12] Jamie Park: for Private we offer customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM integrations, and you can run the private control plane in your VPC or air-gapped on-prem. we'll share the private deployment checklist in the follow-up.
[03:24] Tom Reeves: do you have SOC 2 docs and SAML SSO for enterprise?
[03:29] Evelyn Chen: yes SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SCIM for SSO and user provisioning, RBAC in the Console, and audit logs you can stream to your SIEM.
[03:38] Jamie Park: quick demo of Alerts and Budgets — set a spend budget per route and get alerted at 50/80/100% thresholds; you can also set automatic fallback to a cheaper model if budget exceeded.
[03:50] Priya Nair: auto-fallback sounds risky for UX, but ok as a safety net. can we set canaries for rollout?
[03:56] Evelyn Chen: yes canaries and A/B route rollouts — you define rollout percentage and percent canary, rollback is automatic on error or quality regression.
[04:05] [04:05] Jamie Park: now a slightly deeper slide — routing policies. you can route by policy: latency SLO-first, cost-first, or region-first. in practice customers mix: critical payments route gets low-latency dedicated pool, analytics route goes to cheaper quantized variants.
[04:19] Maya Singh: around capacity — if we pick Dedicated for payments, what's the commitment model?
[04:25] Jamie Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly/annual with configurable burst cushions. we'll put options in pricing doc.
[04:31] Tom Reeves: curious about observability — do you expose traces? we'd like token-level traces attached to our request ids.
[04:37] Evelyn Chen: yes trace hooks and per-token timing; you can instrument flows and join with your request id. the Console shows per-request token timeline and the latency breakdown by kernel/attention and network.
[04:48] Priya Nair: let's circle back to pilot — what metrics should we collect to evaluate success?
[04:52] Jamie Park: good question — we typically track: 1) mean latency P95/P99, 2) cost per 1k tokens per route, 3) model quality on prompt set (pass rate), 4) cache hit rate, 5) error rate / timeouts.
[05:05] Maya Singh: ok that aligns with our PM goals.
[05:08] [05:08] Evelyn Chen: now i'll flip over to the pilot template — short pilot, 2 weeks, instrument 3 routes, ingest baseline for one week, then enable Redwood routing and measure delta. we'll provide a small committed capacity so your traffic is real.
[05:23] Tom Reeves: any red flags running real traffic on hosted? we have privacy concerns.
[05:27] Jamie Park: for evaluation you can use Hosted with VPC peering and data retention controls; if you need full control, Private is the route. we recommended starting hosted for speed unless you have strict compliance.
[05:38] Priya Nair: do you do e2e perf benchmarks we can run? like a 10k request steady-state test?
[05:43] Evelyn Chen: yes we can run benchmark harnesses and share results: throughput, latency distributions, and token-ops. we'll coordinate with your SRE to run it.
[05:52] Maya Singh: competitor question — some of the other vendors lock you into their model catalog. can we bring our own open models?
[05:58] Jamie Park: absolutely. Redwood supports open models and customer-provided weights in Private. our model catalog is curated but pluggable.
[06:06] [06:06] Tom Reeves: about cost attribution — can we attach costs to teams? our finance wants chargeback by product area not just route.
[06:12] Evelyn Chen: yes you can tag requests with team id and the Console provides team-level rollups and CSV export for finance. there's also an API for programmatic reporting.
[06:21] Priya Nair: can you demo a CSV export quickly?
[06:24] Jamie Park: sure — exporting route-level breakdown, includes date range, tokens, model, infra cost, realized cost after cache, and tags. download link will be in the follow-up demo assets.
[06:36] [06:36] Evelyn Chen: small caveat — transcription, there's sometimes, ah sorry, i mean, for extremely high concurrency the infra piece may dominate costs and batching helps a lot — the console suggests batching configs per route.
[06:50] Maya Singh: how is batching configured? does it increase latency for small requests?
[06:54] Evelyn Chen: batching is workload-aware: it has latency SLO constraints, so it only batches compatible calls up to a max latency window. you can tune per route.
[07:03] Tom Reeves: can we set a hard cap on latency for payment flows?
[07:06] Evelyn Chen: yes, you can declare an SLO and route policy will prioritize low-latency pools. for absolute minima, dedicated GPU pools are recommended.
[07:14] [07:14] Jamie Park: wrapping toward the end — quick Q&A open floor.
[07:17] Priya Nair: one last one: how do we get alerted on cost anomalies automatically?
[07:20] Evelyn Chen: Alerts -> anomaly detection. You can set baseline using last N days and choose sensitivity. it will trigger Slack/email and can block new model versions if spend delta exceeds threshold.
[07:31] Maya Singh: ok great. i'm comfortable with pilot steps, need to align internal stakeholders.
[07:35] Jamie Park: perfect. we'll send the pilot pack, pricing, SOC2 and the VPC/on-prem checklist. propose pilot kickoff 8/25 or 8/26.
[07:44] Tom Reeves: either works for SRE.
[07:46] Priya Nair: we'll confirm by end of day 8/22.
[07:49] Jamie Park: awesome — thanks all. we'll follow up with assets and owners assigned. bye!
[07:53] [07:53] (call ends)
